stories.title: A diet containing Moringa oleifera alters the goat rumen microbiome and improves animal performance: an insight into bacteria, ciliates and rumen anaerobic fungi
stories.description: In the present study, we investigated the impact of Moringa oleifera feed on rumen and fecal microbial communities, including bacteria, ciliates, and anaerobic fungi in lactating goats (Capra hircus). The goats were divided into three groups based on dietary regimes: masoor straw (MS, n = 10), 20% moringa leaf meal (20% MLM, n = 10), and 30% moringa leaf meal (30% MLM, n = 10), and were maintained on this diet for 180 days. Animal performance parameters, daily feed and nutrients intake, fortnightly milk yield and body weight changes, and feed digestibility were measured. Rumen digesta and fecal samples were collected at the end of the experiment, and amplicon sequencing targeting the 16 S rRNA, ciliates-specific 18 S rRNA, and rumen anaerobic fungi-specific ITS1 genes were carried out. Moringa-fed goats showed improved nutrient utilization efficiency, body weight gain (BWG), and milk production. Linear mixed-effect model analysis demonstrated that milk yield increased significantly from third fortnight onwards in both moringa -supplemented groups. In the rumen solid and liquid fractions, a moringa diet increased the Bacillota: Bacteroidota ratio, which could be associated with lower residual feed intake, improved metabolism, and thus better body weight gain and milk yield. An increase in the proteolytic bacterial phylum Pseudomonadota was observed with the moringa diet, which could be linked with high protein content in the moringa and the diet containing it. In the rumen solid fraction, several plant carbohydrate degraders and fermenters such as Coprococcus, Ruminococcus, Succinimonas, Mediterraneibacter, Cellulosilyticum, Butyricicoccus, Cellulosibacter, Ruminobacter, Saccharofermentans, Agathobacter were significantly abundant in the moringa-fed group (Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn’s post hoc test, adjusted p ≤ 0.05). Ciliates like Enoploplastron, Metadinium and Diploplastron significantly increased (Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn’s post hoc test, adjusted p ≤ 0.05), while Entodinium was reduced in the rumen digesta samples of moringa feed groups. The fibre-degrading fungal genus Neocallimastix was less abundant in the rumen of the goats fed with moringa. Overall, these findings suggest that moringa supplementation positively influences feed digestion, nutrient intake, body weight gain, and milk yield, possibly through modulating rumen microbial communities in the lactating goats. These findings also highlight the complex interactions between moringa-based diet and rumen microbes, which may further improve goat health and milk production. However, future experiments focusing on the analysis of phytochemical composition of moringa leaves and rumen fermentation parameters would further strengthen these findings.

stories.title: Network-based gene prioritization using hybrid scoring for complex disease module discovery
stories.description: Complex diseases arise from perturbations in interconnected biological networks rather than isolated genetic defects. Network-based approaches provide a systematic framework for understanding disease mechanisms through protein-protein interaction data, yet most existing methods are developed and validated on a single disease or pathogenic mechanism, leaving their generalizability largely untested. We present a disease-agnostic computational framework that integrates five biological databases to construct robust ground truth gene sets, applies sensitivity analysis to identify high-confidence disease genes, and combines network topology with diffusion algorithms for systematic gene prioritization, requiring only a disease name as input. Our approach employs a noisy-OR fusion strategy to integrate evidence from DISEASES, GeneCards, OpenTargets, Gene2Phenotype, and NCBI Gene, followed by genetic algorithm optimization and random walk with restart for gene prioritization. Disease-relevant subnetworks were extracted and analyzed using complementary clustering algorithms (Leiden and MCL) to identify modules validated through pathway enrichment analysis. Without disease-specific tuning, the same workflow was applied unchanged to two neurodegenerative disorders and one autoimmune disease, chosen to span markedly different pathogenic mechanisms: Alzheimer disease (AD), Parkinson disease (PD), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In each case the framework recovered known disease genes and identified biologically coherent, disease-specific modules: in AD, 17 stable high-confidence genes and modules enriched in lipid and cholesterol metabolism and amyloid precursor protein processing; in PD, 17 stable genes and modules associated with mitophagy, ubiquitin-proteasome signaling, and mitochondrial dysfunction; in RA, 20 stable genes and modules enriched in antigen presentation and JAK-STAT cytokine signaling. This consistent recovery of mechanistically distinct, biologically appropriate signatures from a single unmodified pipeline demonstrates that the framework generalizes across disease categories rather than being tuned to any one of them. By prioritizing biological validation through pathway enrichment over predictive accuracy, and by demonstrating consistent performance across neurodegenerative and autoimmune contexts without disease-specific adaptation, the framework offers a versatile, readily extensible tool for exploratory analyses of disease mechanisms, including diseases for which prior mechanistic knowledge is limited. All code, data, and results are publicly available to ensure reproducibility.

stories.title: An interpretable parametric representation and open dataset for oracle bone script: adaptive Arc segmentation and SVG resource
stories.description: Computational oracle bone script (OBS) research is dominated by opaque, data-hungry bitmap-domain deep models. We present an interpretable parametric representation and an open dataset of 1203 oracle-bone glyph forms in which each stroke sub-segment is encoded by three closed-form parameters—direction α, magnitude η, signed curvature κ— each entry carrying a modern-character assignment and, where that modern character is encoded, a Unicode code point, an error-driven adaptive arc-segmentation method via residual-guided splitting, corpus-level structural characterisation, a controllability demonstration, and a resolution-independent SVG glyph set. The representation achieves a median normalised reconstruction error of 0.0021 at ~10 sub-segments per glyph (4× lower than a single-arc baseline); 72.0% of sub-segments turn through less than 0.16 rad, quantifying, for this digitised corpus, the palaeographic view that OBS strokes are simple low-curvature arcs. The release is a single-representative-glyph-per-character vector resource—a complement to primary palaeographic sources, not a substitute.

stories.title: Development and assessment of silver-zinc dual doped silymarin nanocrystals for multifunctional photocatalytic, antibacterial, and cytotoxic applications
stories.description: This research aims to develop aqueous-soluble Ag/Zn-doped silymarin nanocrystals (SNCs) from Silybum marianum extract using the solvent evaporation technique as an innovative platform to enhance the bioactivity of silymarin. The synthesized nanocrystals were evaluated for their antibacterial, cytotoxic, and photocatalytic activities, highlighting their potential as multifunctional silymarin-based nanomaterials. XRD analysis of the Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs indicated amorphous structures. TEM and FESEM images revealed that the Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs exhibited spherical characteristics, with a mean size of about 33.83 nm. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the characteristic functional groups of silymarin and indicated the successful incorporation of Ag and Zn into the nanocrystal structure. The results of the UV-Vis analysis demonstrated that the Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs exhibited strong absorption peaks at 233, 289, and 449 nm. The EDX and mapping analyses confirmed the elemental composition and the successful incorporation of Ag and Zn into the silymarin nanocrystals. The results from the photocatalytic test showed that Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs achieved a 98% degradation of the MB (methylene blue) dye. The MTT results demonstrated that Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs had moderate toxicity toward cancer MDA-MB-231 cells (IC50 value of 389.7 µg/mL). Furthermore, the antibacterial outcomes indicated that the Ag/Zn dual-doped SNCs displayed enhanced effectiveness against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus (ATCC strains) compared to clinical strains.

stories.title: Thinner Gaming Laptop Designs Can Hit Combined 215W Power Limits Through Experimental Utility While Approaching Thermal Throttling Ceiling And Jet-Like Fan Noise
stories.description: Discover how thinner gaming laptop designs push performance to 215W power limits, despite approaching thermal throttling ceilings and producing jet-like fan noise

stories.title: Consultant Says ‘Vulnerable' Indie Devs Overpaid For Marketing
stories.description: Indie developers are complaining about a content creator's expensive marketing package, which apparently results in little, if any, return on investment

stories.title: The rule airline boss always follows when flying long haul
stories.description: The general manager for Etihad Airways in Australia tells Aussies not to plan their journey “too tightly.”

stories.title: The full version of Endless Legend 2 has been released on PC and consoles - the creators of the 4X strategy game introduced new factions
stories.description: The developers have released a major 1.0 update with improvements and content.

stories.title: GTA 6 will get more dynamic shootouts in the style Red Dead Redemption and Max Payne 3
stories.description: An analysis of GTA 6's combat system points to a high rate of fire for weapons, responsive character controls, and sophisticated destruction physics.
